title: Check which desktop environment is running
summary: The desktop environment is the graphical interface you see on screen, such as GNOME, KDE Plasma or XFCE. Its name is stored in the shell variable XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP, and printing that variable in a terminal shows which one your session uses.

prerequisites: A terminal window is open inside your graphical desktop (not over SSH and not in a text console)

steps.explain: Prints the name of the desktop environment that your graphical session set when it started. The variable is filled in only inside a graphical session.
steps.gui: Open the Settings app and look at its About page: it shows the GNOME Version on GNOME or the KDE Plasma Version on KDE Plasma.
steps.expect: One name such as GNOME, KDE, XFCE, X-Cinnamon, MATE or LXQt. Ubuntu's GNOME prints ubuntu:GNOME. An empty line means this terminal is not inside a graphical session.

alternatives.explain: Prints an older session variable that many systems set to the session name, such as gnome, plasma, xfce or cinnamon. Use it when the first command prints nothing.
alternatives.expect: A short lowercase session name such as gnome or plasma. An empty line means the variable is not set.
